svg.aria-label: Kīlauea is refilling the hole it blew in itself
svg.desc: Kīlauea is refilling the hole it blew in itself. Sixty per cent of the void the 2018 collapse left in Halemaʻumaʻu has been filled back in, the observatory says, raising the crater floor 490 metres. The vents are still 65 metres below the rim.
svg.text: Kīlauea is refilling the hole it blew in itself
Sixty per cent of the void the 2018 collapse left in Halemaʻumaʻu has been filled back in, the observatory says, raising
the crater floor 490 metres. The vents are still 65 metres below the rim.

g.aria-label: Two frames from one fixed webcam, one above the other. In the upper frame, dated 23 December 2024, the crater is a deep bowl: a tall banded tan wall stands well above a dark sunken floor. In the lower frame, dated 27 June 2026, that floor has risen into a wide flat grey plain and the wall above it is far shorter. A small red lava fountain plays at the left edge of both frames.
g.desc: Two frames from one fixed webcam, one above the other. In the upper frame, dated 23 December 2024, the crater is a deep bowl: a tall banded tan wall stands well above a dark sunken floor. In the lower frame, dated 27 June 2026, that floor has risen into a wide flat grey plain and the wall above it is far shorter. A small red lava fountain plays at the left edge of both frames.

g.aria-label: An aerial view down into a wide grey crater whose western floor is covered edge to edge with fresh black lava; the left of the frame is brown with tephra fallout and a broken section of former road is visible at lower right.
g.desc: An aerial view down into a wide grey crater whose western floor is covered edge to edge with fresh black lava; the left of the frame is brown with tephra fallout and a broken section of former road is visible at lower right.

g.aria-label: A wide panorama across the crater from its northwest rim: a bright orange lava fountain jets from a vent on the far side while a glowing flow runs left to right along the near edge of the black crater floor.
g.desc: A wide panorama across the crater from its northwest rim: a bright orange lava fountain jets from a vent on the far side while a glowing flow runs left to right along the near edge of the black crater floor.
g.text: north vent fountaining into the crater.

svg.text: Photographs: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory, public domain. Figures quoted from USGS HVO, “Volcano Watch — When will
Halemaʻumaʻu fill with lava?”, 16 July 2026 — nothing here is computed by us. Buried Signals · 23 August 2026.
